sources.citation: Blevins, Juliette. 2025. Linguistically motivated sound change (ch. 4) in Kuznetsova, Anderson et al. (eds.), Rarities in phonetics and phonology. Berlin: Language Science Press (book 415).
sources.note: Keninjal cited only as lexical comparanda (jalan, kemayaŋ, kumaŋ) in a discussion of Iban final nasals; the 'stress is consistently word-final' sentence there concerns Iban, not Keninjal.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. (Keninjal primary wordlist, consultant at Kota Baru on the Pinoh River; secs 2.8.1-2.8.3 pp.183-193.)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: No Keninjal-specific statement. Only an areal remark, sec. 2.8.2 (p.184/185): 'Most importantly, stress in many of the languages of West Kalimantan is consistently word-final, a feature of most of the Land Dayak languages of the Kapuas River area' -- said of 'the Ibanic languages.. and other Malayic Dayak languages'; Keninjal is not named and its wordlist forms carry no stress marks. Keninjal sections cover *R > [ɣ], velar fronting after *i, sporadic final glottal stop shared with Ibanic.

sources.citation: Erlewine, Michael Yoshitaka & Carly J. Sommerlot. 2025. Voice and extraction in Malayic. LingBuzz 007614 (accepted, Language).
sources.note: Does not mention Keninjal at all (checked full text; file not kept).

sources.citation: Sommerlot, Carly J. 2020. On the syntax of West Kalimantan: Asymmetries and A'-movement in Malayic and Land Dayak languages. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. xvi+284 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog's only 'descriptive' reference for keni1248, but Keninjal appears only in comparative sound-change tables taken from Smith 2017 (e > o in the penult, *R reflexes) and in a remark that no work on Keninjal passives is known; 'stress' occurs only in the non-phonological sense. Not a description of Keninjal.

sources.citation: Juliarsa; Sesilya Saman; Paternus Hanye. 2014. Afiksasi Bahasa Dayak Keninjal. Jurnal Pendidikan dan Pembelajaran Khatulistiwa (JPPK) 3(6), 13 pp. doi:10.26418/jppk.v3i6.5975 (Untan, Pontianak).
sources.note: Nothing. Morphology only (prefixes be-, se-, N-, pe-, peN-, te-, infix -en-) for the Keninjal of Desa Bina Jaya, Kec. Tanah Pinoh, Kab. Melawi; a full-text search for stress/accent tekanan/aksen/stres/suprasegmental = nil; bibliography cites no earlier Keninjal description.

sources.citation: Meyers, Jim, Ben Rice, Susan Rice & Heather Meyers. 2003. Report on the Seruyan River surveys in Central Kalimantan: Kohin, Keninjal and Sebaun (Dohoi) languages. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-017. 18 pp.
sources.note: Open-access SIL survey with Keninjal wordlists (Seruyan-river Keninjal, Central Kalimantan side); low probability of a stress remark but it is the only other primary Keninjal source

sources.citation: Anderbeck, Karl Ronald. 2018. Mapping the dialect network of Western Bornean Malayic. PhD dissertation, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (National University of Malaysia). 452 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 94610)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only large modern first-hand survey of the Melawi-basin Malayic dialects (Keninjal, Kubing etc.); dialect-mapping theses of this kind usually include transcription conventions and phonetic notes where a final- vs penultimate-stress remark for Keninjal would appear. SIL lists it 'Not Available Online'; UKM thesis repository or the author.

sources.citation: Any Universitas Tanjungpura (FKIP, Pontianak) or Balai Bahasa Kalimantan Barat skripsi/report titled 'Fonologi Bahasa Dayak Keninjal' (none located; Untan OJS, Garuda and CrossRef searched: only Juliarsa et al. 2014 'Afiksasi', Idayani et al. 2018 'Peribahasa', and a 2020 'Leksikon' article exist online).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Indonesian student phonologies of West Kalimantan Dayak languages routinely include a 'tekanan' paragraph; if one exists for Keninjal it would be the first first-hand statement. Would require Untan library catalogue access.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 2004. Ibanic languages in Kalimantan Barat, Indonesia: exploring nomenclature, distribution and characteristics. Borneo Research Bulletin 35: 17-47.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Collins led the ATMA-UKM Melawi-basin fieldwork project; this paper characterises the Melawi Malayic/Ibanic isolects (Keninjal is discussed as a putative Ibanic member per Smith 2017 and Sommerlot 2020) and may state their final-syllable prominence.

sources.citation: Hudson, Alfred B. 1970. A note on Selako: Malayic Dayak and Land Dayak languages in Western Borneo. Sarawak Museum Journal 18 (36-37): 301-318.
